title: Buffalo Trace
nose: Vanilla, brown sugar, and mint with a subtle spiciness.
palate: Brown sugar and spice, balanced with oak, toffee, and dark fruit.
tastingSource: Buffalo Trace Distillery official product notes

confidence.note: Buffalo Trace Distillery confirms it uses two mash bills but does not publish exact percentages to consumers. This low-rye recipe (used for Buffalo Trace, Eagle Rare, and others in that family) is the figure most consistently cited across whiskey trade writing, not an official distillery number.

title: Four Roses Single Barrel
palate: Full-bodied and mellow, with red berries, caramel, and a spicy rye kick.
tastingSource: Four Roses Distillery official product notes

confidence.note: Four Roses is unusually transparent about its process, publicly documenting both of its mash bills (a 75/20/5 recipe and this 60/35/5 high-rye recipe) and which of its ten bourbon recipes go into each product. Single Barrel is built from recipe OBSV - this mash bill with the V yeast strain.

tastingSource: Common tasting note consensus (whiskey trade press)

confidence.note: Blanton's is drawn from Buffalo Trace's second, higher-rye mash bill, but Sazerac has never published its exact percentages the way it hasn't for Mash Bill #1 either. These figures are an approximation based on the range most often reported by whiskey writers - treat them as a starting estimate, not a distillery-confirmed recipe.
